summary: August Tholuck (1799–1877) worked in religious studies and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (1816–1820), where he held a post from ~1820 to 1826, before serving at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1826–1877).

August Wilhelm von Schlegel (1767–1845) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Göttingen (1786–1791) under Heyne and Bürger, and later under Chézy and Hamilton. He held professorships at the University of Jena and the University of Bonn.

Auguste Barth (1834–1916) was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. After earning his licence at the University of Strasbourg (~1853–1856), he held a post at Collège Poincaré Saverne (~1856–1861) and was later a member of the Institut de France.
Auguste Comte (1798–1857) was a philosopher. He completed his education at Lycée Joffre until 1814 and then studied at the École polytechnique from 1814 to 1816.

Augustus Frederic Rudolf Hoernle (1841–1918) worked in Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He served as Direttore at Aliah University (~1881–1895) and as secretary of The Asiatic Society in 1891.

Awadh Kishore Narain (1925–2013) specialized in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and at SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, later holding professorships at Banaras Hindu University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1971–1987).

Axel Klein (born 1968) specializes in Japanology. He studied at the University of Bonn (1987–1994), where he worked from 1998 to 2007. He later held posts at the German Institute for Japanese Studies and the University of Duisburg-Essen.

Axel Michaels (born 1949) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg and Kiel University. He held professorships at Kiel University, the University of Bern, and Heidelberg University, and directed the Nepal Research Centre.

Ayako Nakamura specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She received her PhD from the University of Hamburg (attested 2009), where she also served as a research fellow (attested 2026).

Ayu Khandro (1839–1953) was active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under prominent teachers including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé, Drodul Pawo Dorje, Nyala Pema Dündul, and Chokgyur Lingpa.

Ayya Khema (1923–1997) was active in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under teachers including Phra Khantipalo, Ajahn Singtong, Ajahn Maha Bua, Narada Maha Thera, and Matara Sri Nyanarama, and taught at Buddha-Haus from 1989.
Azizah Nur is a doctoral student at the Australian National University (attested 2026), where she conducts her studies under the supervision of Assa Doron.

B. Alan Wallace (born 1950) works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied at Amherst College and Stanford University under Carl Bielefeldt, taught at Tibet Institute Rikon, and served as a lecturer at UC Santa Barbara.

B. B. Lal (1921–2022) was an archaeologist and Indologist. Educated at the University of Allahabad, he trained under Mortimer Wheeler, served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972), and directed the Indian Institute of Advanced Study.

B. N. K. Sharma (1909–2005) worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Madras and under Satyadhyana Tirtha. His career included posts at Annamalai University, Rajah's College, and Ramnarain Ruia Autonomous College (1953–1969).

B. R. Ambedkar (1891–1956) worked in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned degrees from the University of Mumbai, Columbia University, and the London School of Economics, and held posts including professor at Sydenham College and principal of Government Law College, Mumbai.

id: P:Ba Tur Khenpo Tubten Chö Pel
summary: Ba Tur Khenpo Tubten Chö Pel studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje, and he taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Baatr U. Kitinov works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He earned his PhD at Moscow State University and serves as Associate Professor of World History at Peoples' Friendship University of Russia.

Bahadur Chand Chhabra (born 1908) worked in Indology and archaeology. He studied at the University of the Punjab and Leiden University. He served in the Archaeological Survey of India (1935–1966) and as professor at Panjab University (~1965–1969).

Bai Su (1922–2018) was a scholar of archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He completed graduate studies at Peking University (1940–1944) under teachers including Chengjun Feng and Yongtong Tang, and served as a professor there from 1948 to 2004.
